findings.source_passage: not only did each of these famous whales enjoy great individual celebrity—Nay, you may call it an ocean-wide renown; not only was he famous in life and now is immortal in forecastle stories after death, but he was admitted into all the rights, privileges, and distinctions of a name; had as much a name indeed as Cambyses or Cæsar.
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'But not only did each of these famous whales'
findings.why_it_matters: This passage establishes the grand rhetorical framing — whales granted the dignities of Caesar and Cambyses — that makes the named-whale roll call (Timor Tom, Don Miguel, etc.) interpretively weighty rather than merely anecdotal; the draft preserves the roll call but strips the ennobling preamble entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the 'ocean-wide renown… admitted into all the rights, privileges, and distinctions of a name; had as much a name as Cambyses or Cæsar' sentence before the 'Was it not so' anaphora, even in compressed form.

findings.source_passage: his aspect was most horrible, and such as indicated resentment and fury… the whole circumstances taken together, all happening before my own eyes, and producing, at the time, impressions in my mind of decided, calculating mischief, on the part of the whale
findings.source_locator: Chace footnote / extended quotation after Essex account
findings.why_it_matters: Melville's extended Chace quotations — including 'decided, calculating mischief' and the nighttime boat reflection on 'the horrid aspect and revenge of the whale' — are primary-source witnesses to the whale's intentionality, which is the chapter's interpretive crux; the draft collapses them to a single truncated sentence.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore at minimum the 'decided, calculating mischief' and 'the dismal looking wreck, and the horrid aspect and revenge of the whale, wholly engrossed my reflections' passages from Chace, as these carry the burden of proof for the whale's malice.

findings.source_passage: Like some poor devils ashore that happen to know an irascible great man, they make distant unobtrusive salutations to him in the street, lest if they pursued the acquaintance further, they might receive a summary thump for their presumption.
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'Secondly: It is well known in the Sperm Whale Fishery'
findings.why_it_matters: The simile is preserved verbatim, which is good; however, the preceding sentence explaining the logic — 'that from the fatal experiences of the fishery there hung a terrible prestige of perilousness about such a whale as there did about Rinaldo Rinaldini' — is dropped, removing the named pop-cultural reference (Rinaldo Rinaldini) that characterises the Melvillean digressive register.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'as there did about Rinaldo Rinaldini' or at minimum the 'fatal experiences… terrible prestige' framing before the poor-devils simile.

findings.source_passage: In that up and down manly book of old-fashioned adventure, so full, too, of honest wonders—the voyage of Lionel Wafer, one of ancient Dampier's old chums
findings.why_it_matters: Melville's affectionate characterisation of Wafer's book ('up and down manly… full of honest wonders') is a register-defining aside that the draft collapses to 'Lionel Wafer, Dampier's chum'; the voice texture is thinned.
findings.suggested_fix: Retain 'that up and down manly book of old-fashioned adventure, so full of honest wonders' as it costs almost nothing in word count and preserves the narrative voice.

findings.source_passage: Captain Pollard once more sailed for the Pacific in command of another ship, but the gods shipwrecked him again upon unknown rocks and breakers… forswearing the sea, he has never tempted it since. At this day Captain Pollard is a resident of Nantucket.
findings.why_it_matters: Pollard's second shipwreck and his presence as a living Nantucket resident grounds the Essex story in verifiable, present-day reality, which is the rhetorical purpose of the entire chapter; its omission slightly weakens the chapter's evidentiary argument.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a single sentence noting Pollard's second wreck and his current Nantucket residence to reinforce the 'living testimony' framework.

summary: No high-severity failures; three medium findings involve the erasure of the 'Cambyses or Caesar' ennobling preamble, the near-complete loss of Chace's key 'calculating mischief' and nighttime-boat quotations, and the dropped Rinaldo Rinaldini reference — all of which flatten interpretive and voice-defining material but do not individually constitute full signature loss requiring regeneration.
